content.doc_md:
## Tutorials

The DEGREES() function converts a value in radians to degrees.

Note:See also theRADIANS()andPI()functions.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT DEGREES(1.5);

---

DEGREES(
number
)

---

SELECT DEGREES(PI()*2);
```

## Tutorials

The EXP() function returns e raised to the power of a specified number.

The constant e (2.718281...), is the base of natural logarithms.

Note:See also theLOG()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT EXP(1);

---

EXP(
number
)

---

SELECT EXP(2);
```

## Tutorials

The FLOOR() function returns the largest integer value that is smaller than 
or equal to a number.

Tip:Also look at theCEILING()andROUND()functions.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT FLOOR(25.75) AS FloorValue;

---

FLOOR(
number
)

---

SELECT FLOOR(25) AS FloorValue;

---

SELECT FLOOR(-13.5) AS FloorValue;
```

## Tutorials

The LOG() function returns the natural logarithm of a specifiednumber, or the logarithm of 
thenumberto the 
specifiedbase.

From SQL Server 2012, you can also change the base of the 
logarithm to another value by using the optional base parameter.

Note:Also look at theEXP()function.

OR:

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LOG(2);

---

LOG(
number, base
) -- Syntax for SQL Server

---

LOG(
number
) -- Syntax for Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Data Warehouse, Parallel Data Warehouse

---

SELECT LOG(2, 4);
```

## Tutorials

The LOG10() function returns the natural logarithm of a number to base 10.

Note:Also look at theLOG()function.

### Code Examples

```
SELECT LOG10(2);

---

LOG10(
number
)

---

SELECT LOG10(4.5);
```
